cube_scene.description: A configurable cube scene used as reference geometry across the project. Its variants can be grabbed, scaled, subdivided, snapped, or augmented, but the cube remains the stable primitive beneath those state changes. That makes it ideal for seeing what a transformation preserves and what it alters. In the transformation sequence it functions as the baseline form against which other changes read clearly.
interactions: grab cube variants and move them through space
compare scaled, subdivided, and snapped cube behaviors
attach or detach auxiliary utilities where present
use the cube as a baseline reference for other transformed forms
cube_scene.name: Basic Cube Scene
cube_scene.qfep_connection: Transformation changes S while the cube serves as the invariant reference body. Because the base form is so legible, every modification becomes easy to compare against it.

player_trace.description: A recorder that turns the player's motion into a visible line in space. Every step writes another point, so translation through the room becomes geometry rather than a forgotten action. The artifact makes path and trajectory tangible, especially when compared against grids and axis-constrained motion. It turns movement into a time-indexed drawing.
interactions: walk through space to extend the trace
change trail_length to keep more or less motion history
compare your recorded path against grid or axis demonstrations
use the line as a visible record of translation over time
player_trace.name: player_trace
player_trace.qfep_connection: Transformation is recorded here as a trajectory through S over time. The body changes position continuously, while the trace preserves that history as form.

Rotating or scaling it changes which faces dominate the view, so the artifact makes orientation and aspect easier to read. It is a reminder that transformations act on more than boxes. The prism broadens the learner's sense of what can stay invariant under change.

compare its silhouette against more symmetric primitives

prism_block.qfep_connection: Transformation changes pose and size while the prism's edge structure stays coherent. A less symmetric primitive makes preserved relations easier to notice.
